Aesthetics
During the life of the mining operation, the presence of mining equipment, exposed earth, open pits, and spoil piles will be displeasing to many viewers. As a result of mining and reclamation activities, the present varied terrain will be considerably simplified. The corrent diverse and varied land surface will have been replaced by a manmade landscape which is smoother and much less broken. The variations in tone and color produced by oxidized red clinker zones and variegated softer rocks will also be destroyed by the mixing process. The resulting landscape will lack the harmonious variety of rock and soil colors.
The present landscape supports a considerable variety of vegetation which enhances the aesthetic qualities of the terrain. Vegetation in reclaimed areas is expected to be much more uniform although diversity is expected to increase gradually as woody vegetation becomes established and herbaceous communities evolve in response to microhabitat conditions.
Existing structures in areas to be mined will be removed. This includes seven structures or groups of structures which for various reasons may be considered positive scenic influences.
